source.note: alpha is the extracted source alpha; the transparent central opening is genuine and the hidden RGB under it is not used as backing

outputs.atlas_alpha: straight RGBA; RGB zeroed exactly where alpha is zero

layout.rendering_scale_note: rail transverse cells are 104 atlas px (26 logical, 52 device px at 2x); the atlas is sampled at native resolution and never shipped as a resized copy

resampling.rail_transverse: source full rail profile resampled to 104 atlas px; 85-95 original source px per cross axis (>=52)
resampling.rail_longitudinal: seamless run resampled to the cell length (1024 top/bottom, 512 left/right)
resampling.fittings: uniform (isotropic) resize preserving the fitting's natural offset from the measured outer corner; the corner's outer rim stays rail material
resampling.lamp: one uniform fit of the whole lantern crop into the cell's inner 96x200 box, centred; straight-RGBA LANCZOS with the original alpha preserved

endpoint_method.note: the trailing source pixels are cross-faded into the leading source pixels so the cell's last column is the source column immediately before the first; no mirroring of grain or carving and no repeated corner fittings

TL.mitre: diagonal nearest-outer-contour selection: horizontal material where distance-to-horizontal-edge < distance-to-vertical-edge, vertical otherwise, so both perimeter contours stay continuous
TL.support: L-shaped stationary support built from the corresponding horizontal and vertical rail cross-sections and combined by a real mitre; outer rim is rail material, inner 64x64 atlas px square (the cap's inner 16 logical px) is transparent

TR.mitre: diagonal nearest-outer-contour selection: horizontal material where distance-to-horizontal-edge < distance-to-vertical-edge, vertical otherwise, so both perimeter contours stay continuous
TR.support: L-shaped stationary support built from the corresponding horizontal and vertical rail cross-sections and combined by a real mitre; outer rim is rail material, inner 64x64 atlas px square (the cap's inner 16 logical px) is transparent

BL.support: L-shaped stationary support built from the corresponding horizontal and vertical rail cross-sections and combined by a real mitre; outer rim is rail material, inner 64x64 atlas px square (the cap's inner 16 logical px) is transparent

BR.support: L-shaped stationary support built from the corresponding horizontal and vertical rail cross-sections and combined by a real mitre; outer rim is rail material, inner 64x64 atlas px square (the cap's inner 16 logical px) is transparent

lamp.replaces: the previous paper-lantern object, formerly cropped from master.webp at LAMP_SOURCE (1430,692,1534,897) and packed top-aligned; the base atlas lamp cell is rewritten only when --replace-cells includes lamp (default: only when the rebuilt cell differs from the base)
lamp.transform: atlas_px = [cell_x + offset_x + (source_x - crop_x0) * scale, cell_y + offset_y + (source_y - crop_y0) * scale]
lamp.resampling: Pillow LANCZOS over straight RGBA; the alpha channel is resampled with the colour, so original alpha and antialiased edges survive; hidden RGB under alpha 0 is purged by the atlas-wide alpha-0 zeroing
lamp.packing: isotropic fit inside the cell with transparent padding on all four sides; the lantern is never stretched to fill the cell

content_lantern.transform: sprite_px = [offset_x + (source_x - crop_x0) * scale, offset_y + (source_y - crop_y0) * scale]
content_lantern.resampling: Pillow LANCZOS over straight RGBA; alpha is resampled with the colour so the original alpha and antialiased edges survive; hidden RGB under alpha 0 is purged on output
content_lantern.packing: isotropic fit of the whole object crop inside the fit box, centred; never stretched and never filled with a background plane

correction.preserved: every base pixel outside the replaced cells, byte-for-byte

omitted_source_objects: the original inward concave wooden scroll-braces are omitted as whole elements, not cropped off; the candidate opening is strictly rectangular
not_claimed: full-master preservation; the atlas rebuilds the frame as a layered structural design from source material
runtime: provenance only; no renderer fields are implied
